key_insight: This paper shows how to animate flowing water in 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, extending a typically static 3D representation to handle dynamic, high-frequency natural effects. In simple terms, it makes captured scenes look more realistic by letting water move convincingly in real time.
problem_solved: It addresses the limitation of 3D Gaussian Splatting on dynamic phenomena—especially fast, complex motion like water—under casual capture conditions where dense multi-view, high-speed data is unavailable.
method: Adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting to represent dynamic water rather than treating the scene as fully static.
Uses a motion/animation strategy tailored to high-frequency fluid motion that is difficult to reconstruct directly from casual captures.
Preserves real-time rendering and novel-view synthesis quality while introducing plausible temporal changes in the water surface.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this expands the practical scope of neural scene representations from static environments to visually important dynamic effects. It improves realism in AR/VR, digital twins, robotics simulation, and content creation without requiring expensive capture setups.

paper_title: Make It Flow: Animating Water in 3D Gaussian Splatting Scenes
